title: Tighten p95 regression thresholds for Runtime LTS gates + document waiver workflow
author: Jonas Weber
description:
Context: As part of standing up Runtime LTS, we’re using perf-canary to gate patch releases with a small set of canonical workloads. During the 1.18 LTS pilot we saw a few cases where p95 latency regressed in ways that were operationally meaningful (tail spikes / backpressure) but didn’t trip the existing thresholds because they were tuned for mainline signal rather than “slower-change” LTS expectations.

This PR tightens p95 regression thresholds for the LTS gate and adds explicit documentation for the exception/waiver flow that Release Managers can use when benchmarks are noisy (runner contention, transient GPU clocking variance) or when a known/acceptable tradeoff is made (e.g., deliberate throughput vs tail trade).

What changed (high level): 1) LTS-specific thresholds: reduce allowed p95 latency regression from 5% -> 3% on the canonical LTS benchmark set; keep p50 at 2% (unchanged) and tighten throughput regression from -4% -> -3% for the same set. 2) Add a minimum sample-count rule for p95 comparisons (avoid false positives on short runs): require >= 20k tokens per scenario before gating is evaluated; otherwise mark as “insufficient data” and require rerun. 3) Add a documented waiver workflow: a single, auditable “perf-waiver” artifact linked in the PR / release issue, requiring approvals from Perf Owner + SRE + Release Eng lead, with time-bounded validity (per patch only) and mandatory rerun on dedicated runners if the initial run was on shared capacity.

Why: LTS customers are more sensitive to tail latency regressions because they tend to run closer to reserved capacity and use stricter SLOs; we want the default gate to be conservative. The waiver process is to keep us pragmatic when the measurement system is noisy—without silently weakening gates.

Risk: Tightening gates will increase failures/flake until we reduce runner contention (tracked in INT-3368). This PR mitigates with (a) sample-count rule, (b) rerun guidance, and (c) explicit waiver process rather than ad-hoc “LGTM, ship it” decisions.

Rollout: Enabled only for LTS release-branch workflows (release/* and runtime-*-lts) and leaves main branch thresholds unchanged.

Test plan: ran CI unit tests; validated config parsing; dry-ran the LTS workflow against an existing baseline artifact; verified the waiver template renders and is attached to the GitHub Action summary.

Refs: ENG-4825 (Integrate perf-canary gates into LTS release), ENG-4821 (Runtime LTS initiative), INT-3368 (benchmark runner capacity).
commits: perf/gates: add lts profile + tighten p95 thresholds
workflows: apply lts profile only on release/* and *-lts branches
reporting: enforce min sample count for p95 comparisons
docs: add perf gate waiver workflow + required approvals
chore: update baseline schema version + back-compat reader
notable_snippets: gates/lts_profile.yaml: p95_latency_regression_max_pct: 3.0 (was 5.0 for LTS gating), throughput_regression_max_pct: -3.0
src/compare/regression_rules.py: require_min_tokens_per_case: 20000; otherwise emit status=INSUFFICIENT_DATA and require rerun
docs/lts/waivers.md: adds waiver template fields (reason, impacted scenarios, rerun links, expiration, approvals)
review_conversation:
Marcus Reed (Perf test suite owner): The 3% p95 limit feels right for LTS, but we should be explicit about what metric we compare (p95 end-to-end vs model-only). Can you clarify in docs? Also, sample count: is 20k tokens enough for the long-context scenario?

Jonas Weber (author): Good call. The gate compares end-to-end request latency p95 as emitted by the benchmark harness (includes queueing + runtime). I’ll add a note in docs/lts/gates.md. Re: 20k tokens—this is per scenario per variant; for long-context we typically hit ~60–120k tokens/run, so we should be safe. The rule is mainly preventing short “smoke” runs from tripping p95.

Claire Dubois (Benchmark methodology): +1 to explicit metric definition. I’m slightly worried about flake on shared runners with 3%. Can the waiver doc require rerun on dedicated runner capacity before waiver is granted?

Jonas Weber (author): Yes—updated waiver doc: if the run was on shared capacity or if the variance indicator > 1.5%, rerun on dedicated runner is mandatory before waiver can be approved.

Allison Grant (Observability/perf signals): Waiver workflow needs an audit trail for release managers. Can we make the action upload a waiver form (even if empty) so the release PR has a consistent artifact name?

Jonas Weber (author): Implemented: the action always publishes a “perf-waiver.md” artifact stub. If waiver requested, it must be filled and re-uploaded (or attached in the release PR) with approvals.

Connor O'Brien (Release Eng lead): Please align terminology with runtime LTS runbook: “waiver” vs “exception”. We’ve been using “waiver” in runbooks. Also, ensure this only applies to LTS release workflows.

Jonas Weber (author): Renamed docs and action summary to “waiver”. Confirmed the workflow applies lts_profile only for release/* and *-lts branches. Mainline continues to use default_profile.

Marcus Reed: Docs update looks good. One more request: add a reminder that repeated waivers for the same scenario should open an infra ticket (runner contention) or a runtime ticket (real regression). Not a blocker but useful.

Jonas Weber (author): Added a “When waivers repeat” section linking to INT-3368 and suggesting filing a runtime perf regression ticket if the same benchmark regresses twice.

Approvals: Marcus Reed approved; Claire Dubois approved; Allison Grant approved; Connor O'Brien approved.
release_notes: LTS perf gates now enforce stricter p95 latency and throughput regression thresholds.
Release managers have a documented, auditable waiver workflow for noisy benchmark results.
Added minimum sample-count requirements to reduce false-positive p95 regressions.
